params.body:
Closes #1109

## What was wrong

Nightwatch 75 (production, 2026-11-17 14:10 UTC): `ErrorException: unserialize(): Error at offset 0 of 3 bytes` in `WebsiteController::dealerIdFromHash`.

The public website (iframe) carries the dealer id encrypted in the address in two forms: `Crypt::encryptString` for the catalogue, the detail page and the mode button, and `Crypt::encrypt` (serialized) for the search form, the model list and the body style list. The controller chose the decryption per route. A string hash on one of the serialized routes is a valid encrypted value, so `Crypt::decrypt` decrypted it and then called `unserialize()` on the bare three-character dealer id. That throws an `ErrorException`, not the `DecryptException` that R S2-5.24 answers with a 404, so the visitor got a 500. No blade builds such an address; a visitor or a crawler put it together.

## What changes

- `dealerIdFromHash` always decrypts as a string and reads the serialized form of an id (`s:3:"123";` or `i:123;`) by pattern, on every route. The `$serialized` flag is gone from it and from `websiteDealer`.
- A valid hash opens the page in either form; an encrypted value that is not a dealer id stays a 404.
- Nothing that arrives in a public address is passed to `unserialize()` any more.
- The docblocks of the two touched methods are now in English.
- Rule R S2-5.24 names the two forms, and the finding is recorded in `docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen/2026-11-17-een-hash-in-de-andere-vorm-geeft-500.md`.

## Tests

Four cases added to `AWrongWebsiteLinkIsNotACrashTest`: a string hash on the model list, the body style list and the search route; a serialized hash on the catalogue; encrypted values that are no dealer id. Three of them fail on `main` with the exact message from Nightwatch. Full suite: 3291 tests green (2 skipped, 1 incomplete, as on `main`).

Pint reports the controller, as it does on `main`: the file predates the formatter and is left as it is apart from the touched lines.
params.title: A website hash in either form opens the page
